edits.content: - LINE TEMPLATE (fill the slots, never improvise). Every call is one line: `{"tool name": "NAME", "required parameters": [R], "optional parameters": [O]},` where R and O are comma-joined `{"name": "x", "value": "y"}` items, or nothing. All three keys appear on EVERY line, even for a no-param call. Decide the full optional list first, then write `"optional parameters"` once. The last line ends `]}`, then `]</answer>` on its own line. Always write the closing `</answer>`. Recent bad lines: `..., "optional parameters": [{"name": "by", "value": "Stage Name"}]}], {"tool name"...` (stray `]` after call 1, so NO calls parsed); `{"tool name": "...", "required parameters": [{"name": "artist", "value": "Halsey"}]},` (no `"optional parameters"` key); `..., "optional parameters": [{"name": "language", "value": "en"}, {"name": "country", "value": "IN"}], "optional parameters": []},` (the second key erased language and country). Rewrite any such line from the template.

- SCHEMA COPY STEP (per call, before writing JSON). In your checklist, copy the chosen tool's `Required parameters:` and `Optional parameters:` name lists verbatim from ITS OWN block (e.g. `Wayfair: auto-complete: Required [query]; Optional []`). Fill every name under Required in `required parameters`, even enum-like ones such as `language`. Put only names under Optional in `optional parameters`. BAD: `News Network: Search News` with `keyword` required and `language`=`en` optional (the schema lists both as required). GOOD: `"required parameters": [{"name": "keyword", "value": "Middle East politics"}, {"name": "language", "value": "en"}], "optional parameters": []`.
- Sibling tools share ideas but not param names. Wayfair auto-complete takes `query` (`q` is Asos's). `Aliexpress DataHub: Aliexpress - Item Search` has only optional `q`, `startPrice`, `endPrice`, `region`, `page` (`minPrice`/`maxPrice` belong to `Ali Express Data Service: Search Items`, and `loc` is not `region`). '$200-$500 in the US region' -> optional startPrice=`200`, endPrice=`500`, region=`US`, nothing in required. Then tick each adjective of the clause against the Optional names: 'English sports news from India' on `News API_v2: Top Headlines` -> language=`en` AND category=`sports` AND the country.
- DO NOT LEAK QUALIFIERS ACROSS CLAUSES. 'Page 1' in the election clause belongs only to the election call. Add `page`, `limit` or any other optional to a call only when that call's own clause states or implies it.

- RANK AND RANGE VALUES. When a clause says 'top N' or 'first N' and the tool has a `range` param (description like 'returns all results if range is not specified'), pass the position span `1-N` (`Billboard_v2: Greatest of All Time Songs of the Summer`: 'top 10' -> `range`=`1-10`), not the words 'top 10'. Pass a plain count to `limit`, `count` or `pageSize` instead. Email-style, ID and free-text inputs stay verbatim.
- ADMIN HIERARCHY DEPTH. For a place hierarchy (Airbnb admin fields), fill levels top-down and put the CITY in the deepest matching level, not a higher one. 'Rome (Roma), Italy, 1 bedroom, up to 2 guests' -> `state`=`IT`, `admin1`=`Lazio`, `admin2`=`Citta metropolitana di Roma Capitale`, `admin3`=`Roma`, `bedrooms`=`1`, `maxGuestCapacity`=`2`. BAD: city in `admin2` with `admin1` skipped, because the tool requires parents to be filled for each child level.

- NOUN PICKS THE ENDPOINT; NO LOOK-ALIKE SUBSTITUTES. 'Republican figures' / 'people' / 'influencers' with a topic and page -> `Election2020 Smartable: GetPeopleByTopic` (`page`=`1`, `topic`=`republican-voice`), not `GetFutureEventsByTopic`. 'Events' -> an Events endpoint, 'FAQs' -> a FAQs endpoint. Never swap in a different outlet's endpoint.
- OUTLET WITHOUT ITS OWN ENDPOINT -> THE BY-SOURCE SELECTOR, NOT KEYWORD SEARCH. If no per-outlet endpoint exists in the list for the named outlet, take the tool whose param literally selects a source, with the outlet as a lowercase slug: 'latest news from CNN' -> `Moka News: By Source (New)` (`source`=`cnn`); BBC -> `BizToc: News / Source` (`source_id`=`bbc`). BAD: `Newscatcher: /v1/search_free` with q=`CNN` (keyword search is for topics). Per-outlet endpoints (`Arabic news API: Aljazeera`) still win when they exist.
- 'Blog posts and news' about one game is ONE call when a single endpoint's Description already names both nouns (`Rocket League: Blog` says 'blog posts and news content'). Do not add `Rocket League: News`. Read the first candidate's Description before adding a call for the second noun.

- TWO VALUES FOR ONE PARAM = TWO CALLS. If a clause names several places, countries, IDs or emails ('COVID stats for both Egypt and the United States') and the tool's param takes one value, write one object per value. BAD: one `Coronavirus Smartable: GetStats` object with `location`=`EG` and `location`=`US` in the same list. GOOD: two objects, one with `location`=`EG` and one with `location`=`US`. Never repeat a param name inside one list, and never join values with commas or 'and'.

edits.content: - COMPARE ACROSS REGIONS = ONE CALL PER REGION ENDPOINT. When a provider has one endpoint per region and the query names several regions, call each region's own endpoint. 'Compare current gasoline prices across Europe, the United States, and Canada' -> `Gas Price: europeanCountries` + `Gas Price: allUsaPrice` + `Gas Price: canada`, each with `[]` required and `[]` optional because none has params. For the US, take the country-level aggregate (`allUsaPrice`), not a city list. Do not merge regions into one call and do not add a region the query did not name.

## Value-form addenda (recent misses)
- Region/country codes taken from the query's place name are lowercase slugs for these tools: `Spotify _v2: New releases` 'UK' -> country=`uk`; `AI News - Global: Get News` 'US region, version v1' -> region=`us`, version=`v1`. Locale defaults (Asos `US`/`en-US`) and Epic Games codes keep the case given in Section E.
